summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style infobox and caption summary of the Orange River, southern Africa's major river, which rises in the Maloti Mountains of Lesotho and flows west to the Atlantic Ocean at Alexander Bay. It lists the river's countries, tributaries, landmarks, source and mouth, length, basin area and average discharge. A map caption notes that the basin boundary is conservative because the Kalahari basin is excluded and some sources include parts of Botswana.
one_line: The Orange River is a long southern African river rising in Lesotho's Maloti Mountains and flowing to the Atlantic at Alexander Bay.
key_facts: The Orange River is also known as Orange Gariep, Oranje and Senqu River.
The Orange River flows through Lesotho, South Africa and Namibia.
The Orange River's source is Thaba Putsoa in the Maloti Mountains (Drakensberg) of Lesotho, at an elevation of 3,350 m (10,991 ft).
The Orange River's mouth is at Alexander Bay on the Atlantic Ocean.
The Orange River is 2,200 km (1,367 mi) long.
The Orange River's basin covers 973,000 km (375,677 sq mi).
The Orange River's average discharge is 365 m/s (12,890 cu ft/s).
The Caledon River, Vaal River and Fish River (Namibia) are tributaries of the Orange River, with the Caledon and Vaal listed as right-bank tributaries.
Landmarks on the Orange River include the Gariep Dam and the Augrabies Falls.
The Orange River is shown in a sunset photograph near Upington in the Northern Cape.
The map caption states the basin boundary shown is a conservative border that excludes the Kalahari basin, which some sources say is endorheic.
Some other sources using computational methods show a basin that includes parts of Botswana and hence of the Kalahari.
